sections.title: A) FUTURE TENSES: PLAN
sections.subtitle: Be going to · Present continuous · Present simple

blocks.heading: BE GOING TO
blocks.formula: AM / IS / ARE + GOING TO + INF

compare.label: Make a future prediction based on an evidence
compare.text: Look at those dark clouds; it **is going to rain**.

compare.label: A future plan
compare.text: I **am going to study** a Master's degree next year.

blocks.heading: PRESENT CONTINUOUS
blocks.rule: A future plan with someone else (appointment). También se puede decir con TO BE + TO + INF.

blocks.heading: PRESENT SIMPLE
examples: The train to London **leaves** at 8:00 AM.
The exam **is due to start** in ten minutes.

blocks.heading: Make a future offer
examples: **Shall I open** the window for you?

compare.label: Universal facts / future factual statements
compare.text: The sun **will rise** at 6:30 AM tomorrow.

compare.label: Make a future prediction
compare.text: I think robots **will do** all the housework in 2050.

compare.label: Spontaneous decision made at the moment of speaking
compare.text: We are out of milk? I **will go** to the supermarket right now.

blocks.heading: Future intention
blocks.formula: THINK / EXPECT / BELIEVE / SUPPOSE + WILL + INF
examples: I expect she **will pass** the driving test.

sections.title: C) FUTURE CONTINUOUS vs FUTURE PERFECT
sections.subtitle: In progress in the future vs finished before a point in the future

compare.label: Future continuous → future situation in progress
compare.text: At this time tomorrow, Álvaro **will be explaining** rules.

compare.label: Future perfect → a past situation in the future
compare.text: By this time tomorrow, I **will have finished** all my exams.

sections.title: D) IMMEDIATE FUTURE EVENTS
sections.subtitle: To be (present simple) + about to / on the point of

blocks.heading: About to / On the point of
formulas: AM / IS / ARE + ABOUT TO + INF
AM / IS / ARE + ON THE POINT OF + V-ING
examples: We **are about to go** on holiday.
We **are on the point of going** on holiday.

blocks.heading: Possibility
examples: It **might rain** later, so take an umbrella.

blocks.heading: Probability
formulas: MAY / MIGHT / COULD + WELL + INF (sin to)
THERE IS A LITTLE / SLIGHT / STRONG / SOME / ANY LIKELIHOOD + OF + V-ING
THERE IS A LITTLE / SLIGHT / STRONG / SOME / ANY LIKELIHOOD + THAT + clause
examples: She **may well get** the promotion; she has worked very hard.
They **are likely to win** the match tomorrow.
There is a **strong likelihood of him passing** the exam.
There is a **strong likelihood that he will pass** the exam.

blocks.heading: Certainty
examples: He **is bound to complain** about the food; he never likes anything.

speaking.structure: There is a strong likelihood that [subject] will increasingly [verb base] in the coming years.
speaking.example: There is a strong likelihood that people will increasingly work from home in the coming years.
speaking.translation: Hay una gran probabilidad de que [sujeto] cada vez [verbo] más en los próximos años.

speaking.structure: If we choose this option, we are bound to face [problem/situation].
speaking.example: If we choose this option, we are bound to face financial difficulties.
speaking.translation: Si elegimos esta opción, es casi seguro que nos enfrentemos a [problema/situación].

speaking.part: Part 2 (Speculating about what will happen next in the picture)
speaking.structure: Judging by [evidence], it seems highly likely to me that [subject] is going to [verb].
speaking.example: Judging by his expression, it seems highly likely to me that he is going to complain to the manager.
speaking.translation: A juzgar por [evidencia], me parece muy probable que [sujeto] vaya a [verbo].

speaking.structure: I'm going to have to say that [opinion], mainly because...
speaking.example: I'm going to have to say that the first picture is more relevant, mainly because...
speaking.translation: Voy a tener que decir que [opinión], principalmente porque...
